cast_dialogue.linea: Heroes, sometimes you don't do the job — you CAUSE the job to be done. 'Have it done': the grammar of delegation.
I get my camera serviced once a year. I'd never repair it myself!
I had my restaurant's windows cleaned before the inspection. The inspector was impressed.
I'm getting my novel printed at a local shop. And next week I'm having my hair cut!
I'm having the kitchen painted next week, mis héroes. At my age, the smartest skill is knowing who to call.

inicio.definicion_pragmatica: Causative: have/get + object + past participle = you arrange for someone else to do the job. Order matters: 'I had my hair cut' (NOT 'I had cut my hair' — that would mean you cut it!). 'Get' is slightly more informal than 'have'.

filas: We are having the roof fixed.

ejercicios.respuesta: I have my hair cut every month. I get my eyes tested every two years. I had my phone screen repaired last year.

guion: Sofía: Your kitchen looks amazing, Abuela Carmen!
Abuela Carmen: Thank you! I'm having it painted this week.
Sofía: Oh, so you're not painting it yourself?
Abuela Carmen: At my age? No, mis héroes! I had the roof installed by professionals too.
Sofía: Smart. I'm getting my novel printed at a local shop, by the way.
Abuela Carmen: Wonderful! And Ben gets his camera serviced once a year, he told me.
Sofía: It's true — sometimes the smartest skill is knowing who to call.
